clips.speaker: Carlos Riz Hernandez
clips.title: 巴拿马前副外长：运河中立能扛住中美博弈冲击吗
title_lines: 能扛住中美博弈冲击吗

subtitles.en: I think it was designed for this kind of shocks. If you look at Panama kind of being able to position itself as a safe haven for transit for these ships and vessels, how does Panama position itself geopolitically to make sure it maintains the optics of being a safe, neutral place to go?
subtitles.zh: 它正是为这类冲击设计的。巴拿马如何在地缘政治上定位自己，以保持安全中立的形象？

subtitles.en: I mean, there was a moment not so long ago where the President of the United States was threatening to invade and repossess the canal accusing Panama of giving an advantage to China. How does Panama balance its relationship between the U.S. and China and now with everything going on the Gulf?
subtitles.zh: 不久前美国总统还威胁入侵并收回运河，指责巴拿马给中国优势。巴拿马如何平衡中美关系？

subtitles.en: What is Panama's relationship with that region as well? And is there anything you're looking towards making stronger ties within the future?
subtitles.zh: 巴拿马与海湾地区的关系如何？未来是否加强联系？

subtitles.en: Absolutely. I think, yeah, this, this last couple of years have been a little bit more of a PR that we've expected usually with all this now, but I think Panama's image has been very clear and consistent.
subtitles.zh: 当然。过去几年公关压力比预期大，但巴拿马的形象一直清晰一致。

subtitles.en: Panama Canal is Panamanian. It operates neutrally. It's open to all flags equally.
subtitles.zh: 巴拿马运河属于巴拿马，中立运营，对所有国旗平等开放。

subtitles.en: And that's exactly for moments like this is how neutrality, why neutrality works, it absorbs energy shocks and guarantees that its largest user, which are U.S. companies, can go straight to do and continue to do their business.
subtitles.zh: 这正是中立发挥作用的方式：吸收冲击，确保最大用户——美国公司——能继续开展业务。

subtitles.en: I mean, I think the whole situation has relied on continuity and not risk. I mean, geopolitical headwinds, they'll come and go.
subtitles.zh: 整个局势依赖连续性而非风险。地缘政治逆风来来去去。

subtitles.en: A lot of what's happened in the last few years, very unfortunate, but the Panama Canal is ready for this kind of things. And I think that's exactly what we've done in the last couple of years, the government.
subtitles.zh: 过去几年很多事很不幸，但巴拿马运河已做好准备。这正是政府过去几年所做的。

subtitles.en: And do you have to remember that the Panama Canal Authority is completely separate from the government. Both institutions work well and when geopolitics and great power competition have come to our shores, we've relied on those institutions to precisely do what they're designed to do.
subtitles.zh: 要记住运河管理局完全独立于政府。当大国竞争来临时，我们依赖这些机构履行职责。

subtitles.en: And Panama on the canal side, we have the Panama Canal Authority has been around for about 40 years and we've been total Panamanian for the last 25 years since the year 2000.
subtitles.zh: 运河管理局已成立约40年，自2000年起完全由巴拿马管理25年。

subtitles.en: And we haven't had any big problems and major situations except the droughts, which are the real constraints, more than geopolitical headwinds.
subtitles.zh: 除了干旱这一真正制约因素外，没有出现重大问题，干旱比地缘政治逆风更严峻。

subtitles.en: I mean, the relationship with the region is excellent. Our foreign minister and our authorities have been coming and going. We hope our relations with Saudi Arabia this year, we're open embassies, we're literally preparing for this interconnected complexity, but great power competition has brought to us.
subtitles.zh: 与地区关系极好。外长和官员往来频繁。今年希望与沙特阿拉伯建交，开设使馆，为互联复杂性做准备。

subtitles.en: We can add other modifiers to that, fragile, tenuous. I look at the reporting overnight, I'm more sure.
subtitles.zh: 我们可以加上其他修饰词：脆弱、不稳定。我看了昨晚的报道，更加确信了。

subtitles.en: An unnamed U.S. official told CNN after the U.S. strikes at the action did not constitute a return to major combat operations for now.
subtitles.zh: 一位匿名美国官员在美军打击后告诉CNN，这些行动目前不构成重返大规模作战。
zh_highlights: 不构成重返大规模作战

subtitles.en: Is this still a ceasefire as you see it, given what we've seen play out over the last three or four days?
subtitles.zh: 在你看来，鉴于过去三四天发生的情况，这还算停火吗？

subtitles.en: I think it is in the sense that the terms are pretty clear, right?
subtitles.zh: 我认为是的，因为条款相当明确，对吧？

subtitles.en: I mean, when we actually see text or get briefed on text of what's in the agreement, there's not a lot of dispute about what's in there.
subtitles.zh: 当我们真正看到协议文本或听取简报时，对内容并没有太多争议。

subtitles.en: And it involves Iran being able to get revenue on the front end through the sale of oil and the wave of sanctions on those sales in return for opening the straight in the end of the blockade and then some period of negotiation.
subtitles.zh: 协议涉及伊朗前期通过出售石油获得收入，并解除对这些销售的制裁，以换取开放海峡、结束封锁，然后进入一段谈判期。
zh_highlights: 伊朗前期通过出售石油获得收入

subtitles.en: I think part of what is going on, David, is that the posturing around what's in the terms of the deal is upsetting the ability to implement the deal and get into negotiations.
subtitles.zh: 我认为部分问题在于，围绕协议条款的姿态影响了协议执行和进入谈判的能力。

clips.title: 前白宫副国安顾问：特朗普言论激化伊朗强硬派
title_lines: 特朗普言论激化伊朗强硬派

subtitles.en: You have, particularly on the U.S. side, I think, President Trump sensitive to criticism and sometimes he goes out and he says it makes threats against the Iranian delegation or he's kind of spinning the deal in a certain way that probably upsets the Iranian hardliners.
subtitles.zh: 特别是在美国这边，特朗普总统对批评很敏感，有时他会发表威胁伊朗代表团的言论，或以某种方式扭曲协议，这很可能激怒伊朗强硬派。

subtitles.en: And so I think what you have here is negotiators have a text, but their kind of hardliners on both sides are probably not entirely happy with the fact that there's a deal at all.
subtitles.zh: 所以我认为，谈判代表有文本，但双方强硬派可能对达成协议本身并不完全满意。

subtitles.en: And then you get these kinds of incidents where there's kind of tit for tat.
subtitles.zh: 然后就出现了这类以牙还牙的事件。

subtitles.en: It's still a ceasefire, unless and until these go beyond kind of one-for-one strikes, there's a very careful discipline, frankly, on the exchanges of fire that have taken place today.
subtitles.zh: 这仍然是停火，除非这些行动超越一对一的打击，坦率地说，今天发生的交火非常克制。

subtitles.en: If you see that start to spiral, then I think we're in a different territory.
subtitles.zh: 如果看到局势开始升级，那我们就进入不同局面了。

subtitles.en: And some of those threats from the President have come while negotiators were literally in the room together.
subtitles.zh: 总统的一些威胁言论是在谈判代表同处一室时发出的。
en_highlights: negotiators were literally in the room

subtitles.en: Talk to us as somebody who's handled some of these sensitive negotiations, how difficult that can be to keep those talks on the rails when outside factors keep trying to push in.
subtitles.zh: 作为处理过敏感谈判的人，请谈谈当外部因素不断干扰时，维持谈判轨道有多难。
en_highlights: keep those talks on the rails

subtitles.en: It's a great question because I can tell you, right, when we were doing communications around Iran nuclear negotiations, sometimes we would go out and talk about the kinds of concessions that we were pushing for at the negotiating table.
subtitles.zh: 问得好，我可以告诉你，在围绕伊朗核谈判进行沟通时，有时我们会公开谈论我们在谈判桌上争取的让步。

subtitles.en: And the Iranian negotiators would tell us, hey, you're creating huge problems for me with the IRGC, the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps, the more hard-line elements inside of my government.
subtitles.zh: 伊朗谈判代表会告诉我们，嘿，你给我的伊斯兰革命卫队和政府内强硬派制造了巨大麻烦。
